## Plotting the result

> Note that I could also choose a similar looking color from [this list](https://matplotlib.org/stable/gallery/color/named_colors.html) instead of defining my own
code_block:
def run_module(ctx):
    import numpy as np
    import pandas as pd
    from matplotlib import pyplot as plt
    from scipy import stats
    import sklearn
    from sklearn import metrics, model_selection, linear_model, cluster, decomposition, preprocessing, ensemble, tree, neighbors, svm, mixture
    data = ctx.get('data')
    from matplotlib import pyplot as plt
    import numpy as np
    
    xs, ys = data.columns
    
    light_blue = np.array([26, 110, 177]) / 255  # RGB value from WPD Color Picker
    
    fig, ax = plt.subplots()
    ax.plot(data[xs], data[ys], '.', color=light_blue)
    ax.set_xlabel(xs)
    ax.set_ylabel(ys)
    ax.set_title('Compression of architected material')
    
    print(xs)
    print(ys)
    ctx['tensors']['light_blue'] = light_blue
